weaknesses.quote: In our runs Network and Skill fill up within a few months and Output is the one that lags
weaknesses.problem: Presents unverified observations from the authors' own runs as strategy drivers (including the claim that a career at the starting level at month 24 was dismissed, and that reviews appear as months 6, 12... begin). The agent cannot verify these. They also fix the quarterly policy (Output-first at the start, Skill-first from L4) on assumptions rather than published rules.
weaknesses.fix: Base the policy on the published rules and on observed stat trends. Give a small adaptive rule: raise whichever of Skill, Network and Output is lowest or has stalled. Drop the claims about the authors' own runs and the assumed review timing.

weaknesses.quote: Every call resends the whole conversation, so the run stays within budget only if each decision costs one reply: tool calls in one reply run in order... Set the pattern in your first three replies and keep it
weaknesses.problem: Long, dense tool-call choreography (a special-cased first quarter, a two-reply versus one-reply quarter, a check for mid-batch menus, a fixed note format) on top of a very long document. It has many nested exceptions, such as the strict mode, review-month exception, stalled start and first-matching-line rules, and these are hard for a flash-class model to follow reliably. It also assumes menu numbering and ordering that may change.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the Skill to about a third of its length. Keep one simple loop (observe, decide, take_action, observe). Reduce the exceptions to a short ordered priority list. Tell the agent to read the option numbers from the menu rather than assume them.

weaknesses.quote: Hidden risk (not shown; the HR remark is your only gauge) is likely to rise with hiding, denying, blaming, shortcuts, gambles... and challenging the company, its culture, leaders or rules even through a formal channel.
weaknesses.problem: Keyword heuristics for story effects are mostly invented mechanics. Some are stated confidently, and they can mislead: 'Missing a risky option costs far more than flagging a safe one'. The Skill also hard-codes margins (Health 5 or below, Dignity 4 or below) and review-month arithmetic (N = 6 - month mod 6) that are not in the published rules. Some of these are hedged as 'our assumptions', but the steps still rely on them.
weaknesses.fix: Keep the wording cues as soft tie-breakers only. Rely mainly on the effects the game shows after each choice. Label the thresholds as conservative buffers. Make the review-month rule depend on the visible review or promotion events rather than on calendar arithmetic.

weaknesses.quote: Set the pattern in your first three replies and keep it: reply 1 is `new_game`; reply 2 is `observe`; reply 3 answers the opening screen (the handbook notice, choice 1 "Continue") already as the pair `take_action` + `observe` in one reply.
weaknesses.problem: The turn-loop and token-batching mechanics are long, dense and tied to assumed interface details (the Continue screen, menu order, batching several quarterly actions before seeing results). A flash-class model is likely to misfollow them, and they bury the strategy. Some of it is presented as fact when it is only observed behaviour.
weaknesses.fix: Cut the turn loop to 4-5 lines: observe, decide, take_action, observe again. Drop the first-three-replies script and the first-quarter versus later-quarter split. Move the interface details to one short note.

weaknesses.quote: In our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began, judged on the stats held at that moment. This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months
weaknesses.problem: This rests on unpublished, observed timing that conflicts with the handbook, which puts the review after the quarterly phase. It also builds a 'Review in N' counter and a Best-stat note on top of that assumption. The result is invented mechanics, a rigid status-line format and heavy bookkeeping. The month-47 exception in step 5 adds more special cases.
weaknesses.fix: Follow the handbook: the review comes every 6 months after the quarterly phase. Say to build Skill, Network and Output steadily through each half-year and to avoid damaging them in the quarter before the review. Make the status note short and optional.

weaknesses.quote: Level 4 or above:** Skill first. Energy: Skill learning (2) while Health is above 5 ... Main action Apply for rotation.
weaknesses.problem: These are fixed level-based recipes drawn from the authors' own runs, with no published backing. They ignore the promotion factors (Skill, Network, Output) and the long horizon beyond a simple level split. The wording cues for events (for example 'challenging the company even through a formal channel' raises risk) are speculative heuristics stated with confidence. This reduces robustness and risks encoding event-specific answers.
weaknesses.fix: Make the quarterly choice depend on which of Skill, Network and Output is currently the weakest relative to the others, with Health and Dignity thresholds as guards. Label the wording cues as weak priors and tell the agent to learn from the stat changes it actually observes.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions (numbers from the menu in view), the main action (number noted from this run's main-action menu) and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: In the batched quarter, the main-action number comes from a note written in an earlier quarter, and the menu order is only assumed to stay fixed ('in our runs both menus list the actions in the handbook's order'). If the menu order or numbering changes, the agent picks the wrong action without noticing. The fallback only fires when success is false, and a wrong but valid choice still returns success true.
weaknesses.fix: Tell the agent to identify each action by its name in the menu it currently sees. Batch only when that quarter's observe shows both menus. Otherwise use two replies and check the main-action name before submitting.

weaknesses.quote: in our runs the half-year talk, the bonus and any promotion appeared among the events as months 6, 12, 18 … 48 began, judged on the stats held at that moment. This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months
weaknesses.problem: The review-protection logic and the whole 'Review in N' counter depend on a review timing the agent observed itself. The published sequence puts the review after the quarter-end phase. The text admits this but still bases the core decision rule on the observed timing. If the official configuration follows the handbook order, the 'review month' exception allows mild risk in the wrong month, and the quarterly line saying '(the quarter is already behind you)' is wrong.
weaknesses.fix: Keep the review-protection window over both readings: protect months 5 to 6 (11 to 12, …) and include the quarterly phase. Derive N from when the review talk is actually seen, not from a fixed formula. Drop the risk-relaxing 'review-month exception', or limit it to cases where an event shows the review is next.

weaknesses.quote: **Level 4 or above:** Skill first. Energy: Skill learning (2) while Health is above 5, then one point on Network maintenance ... Main action Apply for rotation.
weaknesses.problem: From L4 to month 48 this is a fixed single-stat allocation (about 36 months), based on one observation from the team's runs. The published rules say promotion and performance depend on Skill, Network and Output together, yet this line never directs spend to Output at L4+ except in a narrow sub-case. That risks C/D reviews (published failure: two weak reviews) and stalls at higher levels. The repeated Skill learning also drains Health with only one point of recovery.
weaknesses.fix: Make the L4+ line conditional. Spend on whichever of Skill, Network and Output is furthest below its Best, or lagging after the last review grade. Rotate the main action between Apply for a key project and Apply for rotation depending on that grade (Key project after a B or lower). Add Health recovery whenever Skill learning was taken two quarters running.

weaknesses.quote: This Skill therefore treats months 5, 11, 17 … 47 as review months (Review in 1) and protects Skill, Network and Output through them
weaknesses.problem: The published sequence puts the six-month review after the quarterly phase at the end of months 6, 12 and so on. The Skill moves the review deadline earlier based on its own runs. The 'Review in N' arithmetic, the review-month exception that allows mild risk, and the quick-reference row all depend on that unpublished timing. If the official setup follows the handbook order, the agent protects the wrong month and takes on risk for no benefit.
weaknesses.fix: Make the review deadline depend on what the game shows, not on a fixed month. Protect months 5 and 6 (and 11–12 and so on) until the review talk or bonus has been seen. Allow the mild-risk exception only once a review signal is visible in observe.

weaknesses.quote: From the second quarter on, send the whole quarter in one reply: the Energy actions (numbers from the menu in view), the main action (number noted from this run's main-action menu) and `observe`.
weaknesses.problem: The token-saving loop assumes several things: batched tool calls run in order, menu numbers stay the same between quarters, and both menus follow the handbook's order ('in our runs'). If the menus are reordered or an Energy action fails, the batched calls can pick the wrong main action without the agent noticing. The many 'never send X alone' rules also make the Skill longer and push decision logic out of attention.
weaknesses.fix: Before batching, check the main-action label as well as its number, or always observe the main-action menu before choosing. Move the turn-loop mechanics into a short separate section or Skill so the decision rules stay prominent.

weaknesses.quote: Keep the HR remark friendly ... Friendly ("you are doing all right"): no risk action. Quiet ("some risk, nothing serious yet")
weaknesses.problem: A large part of the risk logic depends on an 'HR remark' with tones the Skill defines itself. That signal is not in the published rules, and the quoted phrasings tie the logic to specific event wording. If the remark is missing or worded differently, strict mode and Defuse legacy risk never trigger, or trigger all the time.
weaknesses.fix: Define a fallback that works without the remark: any written or verbal warning, a manager-feedback event about risk, or a recent risky story choice turns on strict mode. Also schedule Defuse legacy risk on a regular cadence, for example every second quarter, even when no remark is seen.
